title: Grateful Dead Live at Avalon Ballroom on 1968-10-13
lineage: SBD > MR > DAT > Sonic Solutions > EAC > CoolEdit > CD

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a peak‑1968 performance featuring a stellar Dark Star, The Eleven and New Potato.
ai_review.review: The recording is praised as crystal‑clear vintage sound that has survived tape degradation thanks to the archive’s digitization. Musically the show is hailed as one of the best of ’68 – tight interplay, soaring guitar work, and standout improvisations on Dark Star, The Eleven, Death Don't Have No Mercy and New Potato. A few reviewers note a slightly abrupt splice before the drums and that New Potato feels average, but overall the setlist flows powerfully.

ai_rating.rationale: Overwhelmingly high star ratings (average ~4.68) and consistent praise for both performance and audio quality across 19 reviews.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Very good vintage sound; tape had degraded but digitization restored clarity. Reviewers call it crisp, A++++, with only minor splice/jarring transition before the drums.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set described as a peak of 1968 energy; second set remains strong with superb improvisations, though a splice before the drums creates a slight jolt. Overall flow is praised as transcendent and representative of the band's late‑summer/early‑fall brilliance.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia's guitar tone described as perfect/blazing; vocal on Death Don't Have No Mercy called soulful and top‑notch.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass noted for feeding off the others, contributing to tight group interplay.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill and Mickey praised for flawless synchronicity; later drum segment considered less compelling.
